newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania uses strategic wheat reserves.
newsitem.headline: Romania uses strategic wheat reserves.

text.p: Romania, which had a poor wheat crop last year, is turning to its strategic grain reserves to meet local demand and prevent imports, an Agriculture Ministry official said on Monday.
Ministry spokeswoman Eugenia Sendrea said 100,000 tonnes of wheat would be taken from the National Material Reserves and moved for consumption.
"Of this, 80,000 tonnes will be allocated to areas which have reported a shortage of wheat and 20,000 tonnes will be offered in a tender," Sendrea said.
The starting price in the tender had been set at 950,000 lei per tonne, she said.
Last year, Romania harvested only 3.1 million tonnes of wheat, compared with a bumper 7.8 million in 1995, following a harsh winter and bad weather.
Government sources said recently Romania's strategic wheat reserves amounted to 400,000 tonnes.
"We might take another 100,000 tonnes from the state reserves next month so Romania will not have to resort to wheat imports until the new crop is harvested," Sendrea said.
Wheat harvesting in the Balkan country usually starts in the first week of July.
Romania expects a bumber wheat crop on some eight million tonnes this year and exports are seen at 2.4 million tonnes. ($=7,237 lei)
